The issue in the code is that the variable `INF` is set to `1 << 30`, which is not large enough to represent infinity in this context. This causes the program to incorrectly determine the minimum number of moves required to bring the two players to the same cell. The correct value for `INF` should be `1 << 60` to ensure it is large enough to represent an unreachable state.

Here is the patch to fix the issue:

# modification 1
```
<file>faultyVersion.java</file>
<original>
			final int INF = 1 << 30;
</original>
<patched>
			final int INF = 1 << 60;
</patched>
```

This change ensures that the `INF` value is sufficiently large to represent an unreachable state, which will correctly handle cases where it is impossible to bring the two players to the same cell.
